E1.evidence: Issue #235 (opened by the maintainer corot) reports that auto_dock_with_safe_keyop.launch "Doesn't move at all. Probably something with remappings and/or cmd_vel_mux"; the maintainer's fix 35682ec changes the remap and states "Issue #235: remap fixed".

E2.evidence: cmd_vel_mux (yujinrobot/yujin_ocs) and kobuki_auto_docking (yujinrobot/kobuki) are separately released packages. kobuki_auto_docking's launch file loads the cmd_vel_mux nodelet and remaps its multiplexed output topic onto the base's velocity input. The provider renamed that published topic: yujin_ocs 2c10cf98 replaced nh.advertise <geometry_msgs::Twist> ("mux_cmd_vel", 10) with nh.advertise <geometry_msgs::Twist> ("output", 10) (kept in 6d2582b7 as the default of a new 'publisher' yaml key). The same maintainer updated the other kobuki launch files to follow the rename in eba43685 ("-    <remap from=\"cmd_vel_mux/mux_cmd_vel\" ..." -> "+    <remap from=\"cmd_vel_mux/output\" ..." in safe_keyop.launch and webop.launch) but not auto_dock_with_safe_keyop.launch. A consumer following a provider's rename is an interface change, not deployment wiring, even though the consumer's fix is a launch remap.

E3.evidence: UPGRADE: cmd_vel_mux runs at a revision (0.2.2) that publishes 'output', while the kobuki_auto_docking launch file still references 'cmd_vel_mux/mux_cmd_vel', the name the provider declared up to f68923d3.

units.name: cmd_vel_mux
units.revision_basis: The report (2013-02-25) names no cmd_vel_mux version. 0.2.2 (b2e0f386, 2013-02-09) is both the groovy-devel head on the report date and the latest release tag before it; it advertises the output on the name taken from the yaml 'publisher' key, default "output", and exports cmd_vel_mux/CmdVelMuxNodelet with parameter yaml_cfg_file. The resolution does not change cmd_vel_mux.

units.name: kobuki_auto_docking
units.revision_basis: Broken: d0bfb126 (2013-02-25T07:16) is the parent of the fix and the last kobuki commit before the issue was opened (07:37); its auto_dock_with_safe_keyop.launch contains <remap from="cmd_vel_mux/mux_cmd_vel" to="mobile_base/commands/velocity"/>. Resolved: the fix commit 35682ec (08:34 the same day), which remaps from="cmd_vel_mux/output".

loudness_evidence: "Doesn't move at all. Probably something with remappings and/or cmd_vel_mux" (https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki/issues/235). A remap whose source name is never used is not reported by roslaunch or roscpp; the mux published on its own output topic with no subscriber and no diagnostic is shown.

resolution.summary: In kobuki_auto_docking/launch/auto_dock_with_safe_keyop.launch, remap cmd_vel_mux/output (the provider's current output name) instead of cmd_vel_mux/mux_cmd_vel to mobile_base/commands/velocity.
resolution.evidence:
The fix commit message reports the resolved composition partly working: "Issue #235: remap fixed but keyop still fails when commanding after
auto-docking", and the maintainer closes the issue with "There'is no problem. kobuki_auto_docking used to disable the motors after succeeding." The kobuki revision is identified (35682ec), but the cmd_vel_mux revision used in that test is not stated in the source.

notes: The robot base driver (kobuki_node, node mobile_base, subscribing mobile_base/commands/velocity) is the third party of the data path; the mismatch is between the name the consumer's launch file references and the name the provider publishes, so the composition is specified as cmd_vel_mux (provider) and kobuki_auto_docking (consumer whose launch file wires the mux). consumer_built_against (broken) is inferred: f68923d3 is the last yujin_ocs revision whose cmd_vel_mux advertises "mux_cmd_vel" (2c10cf98 renamed it to "output"). The consumer's launch file had already followed a later provider rename of the configuration parameter (subscribers_cfg_file -> yaml_cfg_file, kobuki eba43685 together with yujin_ocs 6d2582b7), so between f68923d3 and 0.2.2 the provider also renamed that parameter, the latched topic allowed_cmd_vel -> active, and the nodelet class name (CmdVelMuxNodelet -> CmdVelMux in 2c10cf98, back to CmdVelMuxNodelet in 22e08aeb); those changes are not failed conditions of this composition. The residual symptom after the fix (keyop commands ignored after docking) was explained by the maintainer as intended behaviour (auto-docking disables the motors) and is not a condition of this case.
